title: Bomba Dance Tutorial with Afro-Puerto Rican Dancer Mar Cruz | If Cities Could Dance

method.teacher_system: The teacher introduces the cultural roots and playing area of Bomba, demonstrates foundational steps called piquetes with descriptive names, and explains how to move feet and skirt together to the rhythm.
method.signature: Structuring each move around traditional Bomba piquete names and skirt-manipulation imagery like creating waves or clearing bad spirits.

practices.what: Explain and demonstrate the paseo step where the dancer walks around the circle to announce they will dance.
Teach Marullo by comparing hip and arm movement to creating waves with your skirt.
Break down Abanico Doble footwork, showing how to shuffle feet with the back heel pushing forward.
Explain El Cierre as putting a punctuation mark or period at the end of a sentence to close the dance.
Offer a simple version of La Cuatro keeping hands on hips while maintaining the same eight steps.
Demonstrate La Limpia, asking the learner to imagine clearing bad spirits away from them.

adaptations.difficulty: The full skirt movement for La Cuatro
adaptations.adjustment: Keep your hands on your hips for a simpler version

beliefs.belief: Before learning the steps, you must learn the basic foundations of the dance space.
It is traditional to dance without a skirt and even barefoot.

moments.says: The teacher introduces herself and states where she is from before introducing the style of Bomba.
The teacher defines the batey space where dancers come to perform the paseo before learning the steps.
The teacher breaks down the footwork for abanico doble by instructing the learner to shuffle their feet and push forward with the back heel.
The teacher offers a simpler version of the la cuatro piquete by keeping hands on the hips.
The teacher encourages the learner to jump into the batey and move to the drums now that they know a few basic piquetes.

method.limits: No learner comments were supplied to analyze viewer feedback or struggles.
